     return pluralize(underscore(word))
 
 
+# What titleize() treats as a word when it keeps all-caps words: a run of
+# letters, digits and apostrophes. Combining diacritical marks (U+0300 to
+# U+036F) belong to the word too, because changing the case of a letter can
+# add one ('\u0130'.lower() is 'i' followed by U+0307) and a word must not
+# fall apart just because its case changed.
+_TITLE_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"(?:[^\W_]|['\u0300-\u036f])+")
+
+
+def _is_all_caps(word: str) -> bool:
+    letters = [char for char in word if char.isalpha()]
+    return len(letters) >= 2 and all(char.isupper() for char in letters)
+
+
+def _keep_all_caps(original: str, titled: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Return ``titled``, a word of a title, with the all-caps parts of
+    ``original``, the word it was made from, put back as they were.
+    """
+    if _is_all_caps(original):
+        return original
+    # Otherwise keep only its all-caps parts, like NASA in "NASA's".
+    return "'".join(
+        original_part if _is_all_caps(original_part) else titled_part
+        for original_part, titled_part in zip(
+            original.split("'"), titled.split("'")
+        )
+    )
+
+
 def titleize(word: str) -> str:

     Capitalize all the words and replace some characters in the string to
@@ -371,12 +400,32 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")

+    Words of two or more letters written in all caps, such as acronyms, are
+    kept as they are when the string also contains lowercase letters::
+
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
+
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        return title
+    # The title has the words of underscore(word), in the same order, with
+    # only their case changed (humanize() may drop a trailing "_id"), so each
+    # word of the title lines up with the word it was made from.
+    originals = iter(_TITLE_WORD_RE.findall(_separate_words(word)))
+    return _TITLE_WORD_RE.sub(
+        lambda match: _keep_all_caps(next(originals), match.group(0)),
+        title
+    )

     return normalized.encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode('ascii')
 
 
+def _separate_words(word: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put underscores between the words of a CamelCased expression and replace
+    dashes with underscores, keeping the case of the letters. This is what
+    :func:`underscore` does before lowercasing.
+    """
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = word.replace("-", "_")
+    return word
+
